title: Config-correlated JSON drift hunter and root-cause linkback
creator: Marcus Rivera
description: Build a service and evaluation workflow that automatically detects JSON-structured output regressions and correlates them with recent model/config changes (model version, quantization profile, kernel selection, runtime flags). The feature produces prioritized alerts with field-level deltas and a root-cause linkback that points at the smallest config diff (commit/flag set/route change) likely responsible. This reduces noisy post-deploy fire drills and speeds triage for model rollouts and runtime tuning.
success_criteria: 1) Detects schema-level regressions (missing fields, type changes, field-level distribution drift) with >90% precision on validation runs; 2) Correlates top-3 candidate config diffs for >70% of alerts; 3) Actionable alerts include sample payloads, failing traces, and a suggested mitigation (rollback, canary, or field-specific patch); 4) Integrated with Console alerting + Slack + PagerDuty for P1 regressions
technical_design: Pipeline components: (a) structured-output probe runner that executes golden prompt corpus across candidate model/config variants and normal traffic; (b) field-level signaler computing metrics (presence_rate, type_mismatch_rate, token_length_shift, value_cohort_histogram) and signed delta scores; (c) config diff indexer that ingests deployment manifests, model metadata, and runtime flag changes; (d) correlator that ranks config diffs using weighted attribution heuristics (temporal proximity, delta magnitude, field overlap) and a secondary causality check using shadow-replay where feasible; (e) alert generator that emits structured incidents with sample failures, suggested rollback candidate, and links to PRs and traces. Implementation notes: reuse evals infra for probe scheduling; store metrics in TSDB with per-field granularity; expose a narrow GraphQL endpoint for Console to display ranked causes and example traces. Prioritization policy: prefer high-severity schema breaks (missing required fields or type flips) and regressions impacting high-traffic routes or customers with dedicated capacity. Plan to implement as feature-flagged runtime in 3 stages: dry-run (no alerts), advisory alerts, enforced eval-gate with canary block.
acceptance_criteria: Automated runs produce field-level delta reports on every canary/rollout
Console shows correlated cause candidates with confidence score and example traces
Ops playbook created and reviewed by SRE and PM with two tabletop drills
False-positive rate measured on historical rollouts is <10% for P1 alerts
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-3): implement collector + basic delta metrics, run against last 6 weeks of rollouts in dry-run. Phase 2 (week 4-6): add config indexer and correlator, surface advisory alerts in Console for a subset of internal customers. Phase 3 (week 7-9): enable automatic alerting and integrate with PagerDuty; optionally gate low-risk canaries. Monitor precision/recall and iterate thresholds.
